add.title: LGBTQ rights in South Korea (Wikipedia)
add.summary: One Wikipedia full-text search round surfaced no dedicated article on trans prisoners in South Korea; the jurisdiction's LGBTQ-rights article documents its only prominent trans-in-state-placement case, military rather than civilian: Staff Sergeant Byun Hui-su, a transgender conscript, was compulsorily discharged in early 2020 after a military panel classified the effects of her gender-affirming surgery as a physical/mental handicap; she died by suicide in March 2021; the Daejeon District Court ruled the discharge unjust and reinstated her posthumously on 7 October 2021; and in March 2024 the Defence Ministry recognised her death as in the line of duty. The same article records that consensual same-sex conduct among military personnel is criminalised under Military Criminal Act article 92-6 (up to two years' imprisonment; a gay soldier was sentenced to six months in 2017) and that transgender people are excluded from military service. It contains no information on how transgender prisoners are housed in South Korea's civilian prison system - no birth-sex vs identity placement rule, special unit, or solitary/segregation practice is described. (Last-resort encyclopedic source; fetched and verified.)
